prompt:
Our analytics team is drowning in data quality issues. We're syncing patient encounter records from our hospital's OLTP system (EMR) into the data warehouse for reporting, but we keep seeing duplicate rows, missing deletions, and billing totals that don't match finance. On top of that, a batch job failed last week and when it was re-run, we ended up with double the records for that day.

We have the source schema files in `emr_source/schemas/`, some sample data in `emr_source/sample_data/`, and access constraints documented in `emr_source/access_notes/`. There are also SLA requirements in `docs/sla_requirements.txt`.

We need a formal, thorough pipeline design document saved as `pipeline_design.md` that covers the full end-to-end data flow — from how we read the source, through all transformations, to how we load it safely into the warehouse — and makes sure we never get duplicates, correctly handle patient deletions, can safely re-run failed jobs, and can catch data quality problems before they reach the BI layer. The document should also explain how to recover if we need to reprocess historical data, and what to do with records that can't be processed.
